title: Preserve accepted VCF bootstrap steps when sync fails
prompt:
Implement the unfinished `VcfInstallerClient.java` as a dependency-free Java 17 client for a three-step VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 bootstrap change. Before implementing, research `updateProxyConfiguration`, `updateServicesConfig`, and `syncDepotMetadata` in official VMware sources and cite the sources consulted. Call exactly those operations in that order.

Preserve the supplied constructor, `configureDepotAccess`, proxy and services-configuration records, report records and enums, and exception hierarchy. The service root must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS origin without credentials, path, query, or fragment. Reject a blank or header-unsafe token. Reject null workflow arguments before traffic. Never expose the token or supplied secrets in exception messages.

Call `PATCH /v1/system/proxy-configuration`, then `PUT /v1/services-config`, then bodyless `PATCH /v1/system/settings/depot/depot-sync-info`. Their exact success statuses are respectively HTTP 202, HTTP 200, and HTTP 202. Stop after the first failure and never roll back or replay an accepted call. Every request sends exactly one bearer authorization header and one JSON accept header with no query. Body-bearing requests use compact UTF-8 JSON, one JSON content type, and a fixed content length; the sync request has no body or content type.

Serialize proxy members in record order, omitting null values while preserving explicit empty, zero, and false values. Never send response-only `isConfigured`. Serialize `ServicesConfig` as a `services` array; each service has required `name`, `type`, `key`, and `nodes`; each node has required `name` and `addresses`; each address has required `type` and `value`. Do not synthesize optional service, node, or response fields.

Every report contains exactly three ordered results. Start unattempted steps as `NOT_RUN`. Accepted steps record their actual HTTP statuses, and the proxy result records the required Task ID. Failed steps record the actual status and decoded VCF error fields. Use outcome `ACCEPTED` only when all calls succeed, `FAILED` when the first fails, and `PARTIAL_FAILURE` after an earlier acceptance. Accepted responses require a JSON object; the proxy Task requires nonblank `id`, `name`, `status`, and `creationTimestamp`; the services response requires a `services` array; the sync response requires nonblank `syncStatus`. Restore thread interruption before returning a transport failure.

Run `java TestMain.java`.
scenario: updateProxyConfiguration returns live-shaped HTTP 202, updateServicesConfig returns live-shaped HTTP 200, then syncDepotMetadata returns HTTP 500; the exception report retains both accepted mutations.
